Getting Started > The Gaokao Unified Engine “Heng” (Biochemistry Core Calculus First): Development Plan
Status: Work started (2026-10-29, ordered by the user); the first six engine v0.1 tracks have landed (local repository), integration acceptance is in progress. This page registers the development plan for a unified engine dedicated to China's Gaokao (China's national college entrance examination): mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology four subjects in one — one subject-neutral unified kernel + four subject calculus modules, not four separate engines. The biochemistry education language and engine originally registered on this page are hereby demoted to the first landed subject calculus and kernel verification slice (the Core Calculus Draft v0.2 is its semantic base draft); the remaining biochemistry content on this page (the sole problem, the full-coverage three-layer mechanism, the five-level education grading, the check chain and phasing) are all forms of that slice; for the unified engine level positioning, kernel, and phasing, see sections one, three, and five. This page was revised on the evening of 2026-10-29 through three upgrade decisions: the goal was raised from “core problems verifiable” to full-coverage verification, the architecture was raised from “one language” to engine + language, the object was raised from “biochemistry engine” to four-subject unified engine, and on the same evening the user finalized the engine name “Heng” (for the three meanings of the name, see section one); two further architecture detail decisions were merged in the same evening: the presentation layer is set to three.js schematic level, and the engine world-model layer base is set to sla_ecs (ECS) (both see section three). The semantic base draft is the user's Core Calculus Specification (Draft v0.2) (stored locally at ~/workspace/user/files/core-calculus.md: species / rules / energy / boundary four primitives, C1–C6 static checks, CTMC semantics); this page cites its section numbers and does not repeat its full text. Work was ordered by the user that same evening (for the first landing records, see section five); this page makes no schedule commitment, nor does it occupy a position in the current overall ordering (see page 13). Distinction from the three probes in page 19: those three are “not proposed, discussion only”, while this piece is a development plan already decided and written, and work has started.

1. Positioning and the Sole Problem

Plan object (Revision Three): a unified engine dedicated to China's Gaokao, with mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology four subjects in one. Its structure is one subject-neutral unified kernel + four subject calculus modules (for the architecture, see section three). The biochemistry core calculus (Draft v0.2) is the first landed subject calculus, also serving as the verification slice for the unified kernel — every piece of the kernel (grading, provenance, dimensions, math kernel) is first pressed by real questions in biochemistry, then expanded to the other three subjects. This section first describes the slice's sole problem, then the foundation of the unity.

Naming (finalized by the user on 2026-10-29): the engine name is “Heng (衡)”, English name Heng, with three meanings, each expressing one layer. First, the balance of conservation: the constitution of the four subjects is conservation — energy, mass, charge, momentum — if the two sides are unequal, it errors; the engine's physical kernel is a scale. Second, the balance of weighing: grading is weighing, placing the student's answer on the scale and weighing out its score. Third, weights and measures: the four subjects share one kernel and one caliber, that is, a unified system of weights and measures for mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology.

As far as the biochemistry calculus slice is concerned, this language solves only one problem: making reaction network models that violate conservation laws and the second law of thermodynamics unwritable at the moment they are written. In one sentence: make a model that violates physics error at the moment it is written, just like a type error.

The lesion is in current modeling practice: forward and reverse rate constants are filled in pairs, balancing is done by hand, energy comes from multiple sources that do not check each other — errors such as elements not conserved, cycle equilibrium constants contradicting each other (a permanent circulation in a closed system, i.e., a perpetual motion machine of the second kind) can all “run”, and can only be traced back from anomalous simulation results, and not cleanly. This language's response is to make energy the sole source of truth: rate constants are always derived from energy per Draft §2.2, the user never directly writes a pair (kf, kr); the Wegscheider cycle condition therefore holds by construction, and C2 only needs to check writing that bypasses the construction; balancing and charge are checked by C1 at the moment of writing (Draft Axiom 4: conservation before expressiveness).

From this follows this language's ontology: the checker is the value ontology of this language. The first implementation in Draft §7 has only a static checker and no simulator; this is not a scope simplification but the positioning itself — even if it only ever checks, the problem to be solved is already solved. Simulation, observation, and module composition are a second layer on top of this guarantee.

The Foundation of Unity: The Reduction Chain and Shared Skeletons (Revision Three)

Four subjects in one is not a platter; its foundation is structural. First, the subject reduction chain: mathematics is the computational base of the other three subjects; physics is the foundation of chemistry; chemistry is the foundation of biology. A foundation relationship means the lower layer's concepts appear verbatim in the upper layer — modeling them separately inevitably creates the same concept multiple times, with calibers drifting from each other. Second, the four subjects share the same batch of mathematical skeletons:

  • Conservation networks: node conservation in Kirchhoff's current law, stoichiometric conservation, and conservation of energy and material flow in ecosystems are incarnations of the same “node–flow” conservation in three subjects;
  • Equilibrium and steady state: mechanical equilibrium, thermodynamic equilibrium, chemical equilibrium, and ecological steady state share the same steady-state and stability language;
  • Probability: mathematical probability, genetic probability (gamete and offspring distributions), and ensemble probability in statistical thermodynamics are of the same origin;
  • Dimensions: physics and chemistry share one set of units and dimensional checks, biology follows it, mathematics is the dimensionless base;
  • Rates of change and differential equations: motion, reaction rates, and population growth are the same family of dynamics.

Doing them separately means building the same skeleton four times, with calibers necessarily inconsistent, and cross-subject comprehensive questions (a standing Gaokao question type) would be homeless between four separate engines. Unity is the opposite: the same object has only one identity across all subjects — the same glucose in chemistry and biology, the same “energy” in physics / chemistry / biology, the same probability in mathematics and genetics. The knowledge base is therefore a cross-subject graph, not one library per subject (for the mechanism, see section three); cross-subject comprehensive questions are a native form in the unified engine, not a spliced form.

Full-Coverage Verification: The Complete Form of the Goal (2026-10-29 Upgrade Decision)

User decision: the goal is to solve “all questions can be verified” — with all question types in Gaokao mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology as the acceptance surface. Rationale: Gaokao questions by design come with reference answers and scoring standards (points for hitting key points), whatever has an explicit scoring rubric can be encoded as an assertion set; whatever can be encoded can be judged. Therefore the boundary of coverage is not “formal language vs natural language”, but “whether there is an explicit scoring standard” — and Gaokao always has one. In this language's context, verification is judging an explicitly encoded assertion set, with judgment in three layers, distinguished between layers by provenance, not by coverage:

  • Layer one: core calculus mechanical judgment. C1–C6 static checks and stoichiometry, equilibrium solving — conclusions are constructively derived from physics and mathematics, with no human judgment component.
  • Layer two: domain calculus modules. Small calculi outside the core calculus, each closed, precise, and decidable: genetic probability calculus (alleles, gametes, and probability), the oxidation number convention layer, organic isomer enumeration, experimental protocol judgment (see the table below). After the upgrade to a unified engine, the organizational form of domain modules is the subject calculus layer (physics calculus, mathematics calculus, biology calculus, see section three): layer one is accordingly generalized to mechanical judgment by “unified kernel + that subject's core calculus”, with layer boundaries and provenance calibers unchanged.
  • Layer three: scoring-point externs. Natural-language scoring points such as exposition, phenomenon description, and experimental analysis: the scoring rubric is encoded as structured assertions (required concepts, relations between concepts, typical error forms), judged by an oracle. Per Draft Axiom 5, such judgments must be explicitly declared with extern and marked in C6 provenance as an extern source — totality relies on coverage, honesty relies on provenance: full coverage is allowed, but an extern judgment must never masquerade as a core derivation.

Coverage target and caliber (2026-10-29 decision). Target statement: four-subject question scenario coverage 95%+. This number must be reported with its caliber cited, never bare — the caliber is “scenarios encodable + gradable, and the grading standard is the same standard as human marking”, i.e., including layer-three scoring-point extern judgments, whose results are marked in C6 with an extern source. At the same time, the mechanical judgment caliber is listed separately and archived: purely core / domain calculus mechanical judgment accounts for about sixty to seventy percent, the rest is extern-layer judgment; the two calibers stand side by side, and when reporting coverage its composition must be given at the same time. The denominator of 95% holds because Gaokao question types and test points are a finite set enumerated by the curriculum standards, varying mainly by variation year to year, with a nearly closed scenario space (of the same origin as the finiteness argument in section three). The real bottleneck is not the architecture, but two places: content engineering (the encoding throughput of the question-type library and knowledge base) and the quality of extern judgments. The composition of the residual <5% is also explicitly listed: purely open inquiry, the first appearance of extremely new question types, hands-on skills outside the paper (such hardly exist within the Gaokao written examination).

Caliber correction (same day): in early discussion of this plan there was a conservative judgment that “experiments and exposition are not within formalization range” — that was the result of mistakenly limiting “verification” to the core calculus layer alone, contradicting this decision, and is hereby voided, with this section prevailing. Accordingly, the source of the assertion sets in section two's “exercises are assertions” is the examination scoring rubric: teachers encode questions per the rubric as model + assertion set + scoring points, the system judges student answers, and the coverage is completed by synthesis of the three-layer mechanism.

2. Starting Point: Education — The Checker Is the Teacher

The user set the starting point: a biochemistry programming language, from shallow to deep, covering middle school, high school, and university curricula, able to write and able to check. The checker immediately points out where conservation fails, where thermodynamics is violated, and why — feedback is teaching, the checker is the teacher.

Its form is the same core, graded openness: each level is a subset of the core calculus, with that level's discourse layer; higher levels do not overturn lower levels, they only unlock more constructions and deeper semantics.

Positioning note (Revision Three): the grading table in this section is the education ladder for the biochemistry slice (the first landed module). The grading ladders for the other three subjects will be set separately when their respective subject calculus modules are proposed, following the general grading rules at the end of this section (subset monotonicity, exercises are assertions, graded discourse); this page does not pre-write them; the unified kernel is grading-neutral for the four subjects, ladders are each subject calculus's own education surface.

Three general grading rules:

  • Subset monotonicity, lower levels are never overturned: the single line of conservation runs from L0's law of conservation of mass through to L4's Wegscheider condition — the curriculum's shallow-to-deep and physics' shallow-to-deep are the same line.
  • Exercises are assertions: lower levels use “passing the check” as the question type; from L2, observe assertions are examination questions, judgment results come with a C6 assumption list, and automatic marking and “which assumptions your conclusion depends on” are completed in one go.
  • Error discourse is graded by level: the same error code, different discourse layers — L0 uses the most concrete textbook language (reporting differences element by element: “2 oxygen atoms on the left, 1 on the right”), rising levels gradually transition to matrix and null-space terminology. The Draft's named error codes + merging of homologous errors + remedy hints (such as merging C1-element and C1-charge reports when H+ is omitted) are the base for this grading.
  • The assertion source is the scoring standard: a question's assertion set and scoring points are encoded by the teacher per the examination scoring rubric (see full-coverage verification in section one) — lower levels use passing the check as the question type, higher levels use assertion judgment as the question type, and the grading form is isomorphic to real examinations' point-by-point scoring.

3. Architecture Decisions

Form Upgrade: Engine + Language; Object Upgrade: Four-Subject Unified Engine (2026-10-29 Decision)

User decision: what is to be built is a biochemistry engine, not merely a language; then upgraded again (Revision Three): the engine's object is the Gaokao four subjects as a whole — mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology in one, not four separate engines. The structure is set as: the engine is the ontology, the language is the engine's surface and contract face. The core calculus is the engine's physical constitution — no engine behavior (solving, grading, simulation) may violate it; the language is the sole channel by which people write models and questions into the engine — teachers composing questions, students answering, researchers modeling all go through the language, there is no second entrance bypassing the language directly into the engine's interior. This structure is isomorphic to the existing three layers in this ecosystem: the core calculus is to the engine as SA is to sa_std; the language is to the engine as SLA is to SA — the lower layer is frozen, only establishing a constitution, the upper layer evolves, carrying usage.

Inside the engine there are two layers: the unified kernel (subject-neutral, from day one not bound to any one subject's concepts) and the subject calculus layer (one calculus module per subject — modules, not engines). All the content of the biochemistry engine originally registered on this page hereby becomes the first module of the subject calculus layer plus the verification slice for the unified kernel.

The unified kernel has four pieces:

Assertion and grading runtimeShared by all subjects. A question = model + assertion set + scoring points; the three-layer judgment mechanism (section one) is synthesized here; the grading pipeline outputs a judgment result + provenance report, with extern judgments presented in a separate zone

Dimension systemPhysics and chemistry share one set of units and dimensional checks; biology follows chemistry's dimensions, mathematics handles dimensionless quantities. The argument in section four, addendum one, on the biochemistry calculus is hereby upgraded to a kernel piece
Math kernelSymbolic algebra, exact rational numbers, equation solving, probability — the first link in the reduction chain, the computational base of the other three subjects. Its exact rational number part shares the same implementation as the biochemistry calculus's heavy kernel two (exact rational linear algebra, see “Architecture Decisions” below), not two copies. The math kernel is not outsourced: the basic algorithms bearing judgments must be built in-house — JS floating point cannot be a referee (√2, 1/3 must be represented exactly), and the provenance of the judgment chain cannot pass through a third-party black box; presentation-layer libraries (three.js, JSXGraph) only draw, they do not judge

Engine base: the world-model layer is set to sla_ecs (ECS; 2026-10-29 decision). layola13/sla_ecs is this ecosystem's existing ECS base, originally built for the Verse / game track (see page 17), and from this plan onward also serves as this engine's world-model layer — one base, two domains, mutually load-verifying. Correspondence: entities = objects in the world (species instances, atoms, circuit devices, celestial bodies, allele loci…); components = the cross-subject shared data surface (Energy, Charge, Mass, Concentration, Velocity, Temperature, Composition…) — the same Energy component runs across physics, chemistry, and biology; the “cross-subject shared skeleton” spoken of in section one is, in ECS, sharing of component types, not a slogan; systems = calculus and runtime processes (reaction kinetics, conservation checks, equilibrium solving, grading assertions, all written as systems). Two structural fits: first, the core calculus's “patterns” ≈ ECS queries — denoting a class of entities by component constraints, naturally isomorphic to Draft Axiom 1's “no addresses, a class of molecules can only be denoted through patterns”; second, systems can be parallelized by entity set, on the same road as the simulation layer's goroutine trajectory parallelism (page 13). One boundary sentence: ECS is the architecture by which the engine holds and processes the world, it does not replace the core calculus — the calculus remains the physical constitution; C1–C6 are static analysis on component patterns (schemas) + system-level checks, and likewise for conservation law checks in the other subjects.

Finiteness is the foundation of feasibility. The education positioning makes the knowledge base a finite set: the species and reactions actually enumerated by middle and high school curriculum standards and examination specifications are on the order of hundreds, university general chemistry and biochemistry expand by one grade, still a finite library that can be manually reviewed item by item — the engine's data long tail is truncated by the curriculum boundary. The same holds for all four subjects: the Gaokao curricula and examination specifications for mathematics, physics, and biology are likewise finite enumerations, with a nearly closed scenario space of question types and test points (see the coverage caliber in section one); unity does not change the order of magnitude of finiteness. This differs by orders of magnitude from open-world modeling (a general chemistry platform for arbitrary species and arbitrary reactions), and is also the premise on which the word “engine” is feasible in this plan.

In this form, the original architecture decisions are all retained, refined as follows.

  • The semantic core is brand new, not built on SA. SA is a systems-level machine of registers + ownership; its instructions, memory, and calling semantics have no intersection with stoichiometry, graph rewriting, or CTMC; pressing the core calculus onto SA would make chemistry accommodate a machine built for systems programming, and both sides would break. The SA freeze doctrine is unchanged, yielding to no frontend; this language's calculus (the full Draft text) is its own base. SA here is scaffolding, not foundation.
  • The engineering shell parasitizes the SA ecosystem. The new language is registered as a host kind=language frontend, dispatched by extension, on a par with SLA and slars, with no separate toolchain; the extension is set at kickoff. Surface richness always enters the core via desugaring with auditable expansion (following this stack's syntax lowering discipline); the position of desugaring in the pipeline is fixed construction by construction — for example C5 must hang before catalyst desugaring, because after desugaring the catalytic relation is invisible (Draft §3.5).
  • Implementation language: SLA first. The checker is pure computational batch processing (parsing, graph building, checking, diagnostics), the same class of load as sla convert, the form SLA is best at; implementing one's own new frontend in one's own language gives ready-made distribution, diagnostics, and corpus discipline throughout, and graph algorithms and the numeric surface press exactly on the SLA / std parts that CXU cannot press — the gaps hit flow directly back into the std improvement queue.
  • Two heavy kernels and the sinking rule. Heavy kernel one: molecular graph canonicalization (WL refinement + individualization-refinement backtracking, Draft §7.3; in phase P1 it can first be comparison-tested against RDKit canonical SMILES). Heavy kernel two: exact rational linear algebra (null space, minimal semiflows; floating-point rounding would lose conservation laws, floating point is forbidden, Draft §7.3). sa_std currently has no big numbers / rationals, listed as a small std piece to be filled first at kickoff; if a kernel cannot be sustained in SLA in performance or expressiveness, it sinks per the “core into std” doctrine to an sa_std extern kernel, with the surface remaining SLA — sinking, not changing language.
  • The simulation layer borrows the runtime, not the semantics. Future simulation backends consume the reaction network (data) produced by the network generation stage; SMC needs thousands of independent trajectories, whose parallelism is carried by the goroutine runtime (page 13), unrelated to SA's machine semantics.
  • Suggested pipeline order: parsing → normalization and species resolution (identity is fixed here) → desugaring (C5 hangs before desugaring) → C1–C6 checked in dependency order → network generation (per-species-level reaction records n+ / n−, Draft §2.5); each stage's intermediate products (desugared core, reaction network, stoichiometric matrix) can be exported, problem localization relies on intermediate surfaces being visible.

4. Engineering Addenda to Draft v0.2

The following four items are new in this plan and not in the Draft, to be merged into the specification at kickoff:

  • Units enter the type system (Revision Three note: dimensions have been upgraded to the unified kernel's dimension system, see section three; this item's argument is retained, its applicable surface expanded from biochemistry to all subjects). Dimensional checking is to this language as ownership checking is to SLA: a standard-state factor such as (c°)1−m in Draft §2.2, wrong once, makes the whole rate constant wrong — exactly the bug class dimensional checking is meant to kill. Quantities such as concentration, volume, energy, and time are verifiable at least at literals and at energy / concentration / volume operations.
  • canon identity carries a version number. The canonicalization algorithm's version number must enter the computation domain of species_id. The lesson comes from this stack's .sla-cache: its macro index cache key does not include the compiler version, and old caches once masked new compiler behavior; every canon change changes all species identities globally, and without a version it is identity poisoning.
  • extern oracles must enter the contract face. External oracles of the sequence→folding→function kind (Draft Axiom 5, C6's extern(name) label) must declare signatures and uncertainty forms on a first-class contract face, otherwise C6 provenance propagation breaks at the extern boundary — half of the uncertainty propagation problem in Draft §8 item 6 is this engineering problem. Lesson: of sa_deno's 23 symbols only 3 have .sai contracts, the rest live outside the contract universe, beyond the contract layer's reach. Scoring-point judgment (see layer three in section one) belongs to the same extern class and is likewise subject to this item: the judgment interface and uncertainty form must enter the contract face, and its results are marked in a separate zone from core derivations in C6.
  • The feedback protocol is characterized as a phase-change item, not done in phase one. Once Draft §8 item 3 (the protocol layer reading sampled values to decide the next step) is allowed, the protocol layer turns from an event list into a truly imperative language, requiring an isolation design from the physical layer's stochastic semantics — on the order of a small language's own proposal, not to be added casually. The v0.2 protocol layer remains a pure event list (Draft §1.9, §6).

5. Phased Plan

  • Phase one: engine v0.1 — minimal closed loop first. Criterion revised: only when the knowledge base + checking runtime + language surface are all present does it count as v0.1; the original “checker alone first” formulation is hereby changed — a checker without data cannot verify curriculum questions, an engine without a language surface cannot enter the classroom. Content: knowledge base v0.1 (middle and high school common species and curriculum equation library, element and valence tables, each entry with a C6 source label, cross-verified before entering the library) + checking runtime (Draft §7 check chain: P1 species layer (SMILES parsing, canonicalization, species_id, compared against RDKit) → P2 C1 → P3 stoichiometric matrix + C2 / C3 → P4 C4 / C5 → P5 agent layer + module gluing M1 / M2; C6 does only label propagation, no report formatting) + minimal form of the question and grading runtime (grading with “passing the check” as the question type) + L0 / L1 language surface (chemical formula surface, middle school valence table, two layers of L0 / L1 error discourse). Advance piece: the sa_std big number / rational small piece (sharing the same implementation as the unified kernel math kernel's exact rationals, not two copies). Kernel neutrality enforced from phase one: the interfaces and data models of the unified kernel's four pieces (grading runtime, provenance, dimensions, math kernel) are designed subject-neutrally from day one, not bound to chemistry concepts — all of phase one's implementation is verified on the biochemistry slice, but kernel code must not introduce assumptions that hold only for chemistry, so phase two's subject expansion does not refactor the kernel.
  • Phase two: solving and judgment expansion + first subject expansion batch + L2 / L3. The equilibrium solver (equilibrium composition, pH, hydrolysis) lands, and from L2 observe numeric assertions are fully decidable; observation evaluation uses statistical model checking (SMC) as the general method (Draft §5.2), results with method, sample size, and C6 assumption set attached; first domain calculus modules: genetic probability calculus, oxidation number convention layer; first extern interface layer version: scoring-point judgment connected to the question and grading runtime, the full-coverage three-layer mechanism synthesized by this point (section three component table); the education surface lands the energy block surface, catalyst and module teaching example library (the glycolysis curriculum project as the flagship example). First subject expansion batch: physics calculus lands (mechanics and electromagnetism first — dimensional model equation systems + conservation law checks; circuit graphs + Kirchhoff node conservation); math kernel deepened (symbolic algebra and equation solving expanded, mathematics calculation question types fully mechanically judged); biology calculus starts (the biochemistry reuse part extends naturally with the biochemistry slice, genetic calculus connects first in domain module form).
  • Phase three: four-subject grading through-connected + simulation and presentation + L4. Subject expansion concludes: the mathematics proof layer lands (structured proof assertions + scoring-point extern, judgment level honestly marked); biology in full (biochemistry reuse + genetic calculus + ecological / physiological quantitative models); four-subject grading from then on shares the same kernel, the same provenance and dimension calibers, and cross-subject comprehensive questions are graded natively with cross-subject graph identity. The engine's simulation and presentation components land: the presentation layer is implemented per the three.js schematic-level caliber (for fidelity and the “judgment does not depend on rendering” discipline, see section three); simulation backends include SSA exact simulation, tau-leaping, ODE / LNA, presentation includes concentration curves and pathway diagrams; there is only one semantics (CTMC), the rest are all approximations (Draft §2.6) — multiple backends are accepted by differential comparison, with consistency between network-free SSA and network-generated CTMC (Danos et al. 2007) as the benchmark. Domain modules add organic isomer enumeration. The education surface completes the full L4 form. Subject order provisional: except for “kernel neutrality + biochemistry first” being decided, the expansion order of physics, mathematics, and biology between this phase and phase two is a provisional order, to be decided again when each phase is proposed.

First landing record (evening of 2026-10-29, engine v0.1 six tracks). On the evening the user ordered work to start, the first physical objects of phase one's minimal closed loop landed in six parallel tracks in the local repository ~/workspace/heng/ (no remote repository created; the six tracks' commit chain e266fac..47a53ee), track by track as follows:

  • found exact numbers and dimensions: exact rational numbers and the dimension system (SLA implementation), zero floating point throughout judgment — the foundation of the unified kernel's math kernel and dimension piece landed first.
  • species species layer: SMILES parsing, canonicalization, and species_id — CCO and OCC have the same id, Kekulé writing is normalized, enantiomers are distinguishable, acceptance 20/20.
  • check C1 checking: balancing checks + rational balancing solving + valence checks + reaction type judgment (the first form of Draft §7's check chain), acceptance 23/23.
  • kb knowledge base: 278 curriculum species and equations entered the library; 109 equations verified item by item by the validator for element and charge conservation. The validator was originally written in Python; after the user set “Python forbidden” that same evening, it has been ported to SLA (see section six).
  • grade grading runtime: the minimal grading form of question = model + assertion set + scoring points, three-assertion judgment and command-line entry complete, sample question package acceptance 8/8.
  • lang language surface: .heng surface grammar frozen + parser + graded teaching diagnostics, 14 example comparisons all passing.

With the six tracks complete, that is the first physical objects of the phase-one criterion (knowledge base + checking runtime + language surface, plus the minimal form of the grading runtime); only after the six tracks' integration acceptance (cross-track contract alignment, end-to-end examples through-connected) will v0.1 count as closed.

Acceptance discipline follows this repository's general rules: examples at each level are at the same time regression corpora (Draft §7.2 already set this precedent); check-class fixes must carry a minimal reproduction corpus, and be verified on an independent baseline tree for “fails before the fix, passes after the fix”; suite readings compare the failing name set, not pass / fail counts.

6. Status

Work started. The upgrade decision chain from the evening of 2026-10-29 has all been merged into this page: full-coverage verification (including the dual-caliber definition of the 95%+ coverage target, see section one), engine + language, the four-subject-in-one unified engine (Revision Three), and two architecture detail decisions — the presentation layer set to three.js schematic level, the world-model layer base set to sla_ecs (both see section three); the same evening at 22:40, the user finalized the engine name “Heng” (for the three meanings of the name, see section one); at 22:41, the presentation / interaction layer added JSXGraph for two dimensions, and the math kernel not outsourced was decided (both see section three). Two further decisions later that evening: at 22:43, the user ordered work to start — the “not started” status is hereby overturned, the first six engine v0.1 tracks all landed that evening (local repository, for the first landing record see section five), integration acceptance in progress; at 22:55, the user set “Python forbidden” — this engine's tools, validators, and scripts are all implemented in SLA, and the kb knowledge base track's validator has been ported from Python to SLA per this rule. This page still makes no schedule commitment; this plan does not occupy a position in the current overall ordering (ordering one grammar batch → ordering two three-machine rework → ordering three Verse / STM). Subsequent revisions to the semantic base Draft v0.2 (ionic strength correction, pseudo-isomer groups, and other v0.3 items listed in its §8) evolve with the Draft itself and are not tracked on this page.

kb concurrency closing (2026-10-30): the mirror re-verification for the kb subsystem's concurrency rework is complete and closed — species dual backends 20/20, kb test_json PASS on SAB, found test_quantity 5/5 PASS on the box, validate_kb box build + run RESULT ALL PASS (the grade batch concurrency was closed earlier, byte-identical to the sequential version). The sole caliber difference is registered truthfully: the validate_kb report differs from the gold-standard md5, only in the INFO count lines — the concurrent version reports by shard (70+1 / 18+38 / 16+52), summing exactly to the gold standard's aggregates 71 / 56 / 68, the rest byte-identical; the gold standard is a product of the sequential version era (entered the Heng repository at edd2693, not regenerated after the concurrency rewrite ffcb114), belonging to Heng-side stale gold standard / emission form, not a compiler defect, not entering the DEF track. Separately, validate_kb's (SAB build) task stack requirement is in (2MiB, 4MiB], vs the default 256 KiB, belonging to the capacity surface of the compiler track's DEF-R2 / DEF-4 family (see section seventeen of page 13), not to be treated as a kb-side problem. The Heng repository has moved to GitHub layola13/slaheng and completed its first push and README status update (main e546168, verified consistent by local ls-remote). Phase-two remaining items (C2 thermodynamic consistency, kb energy data collection, canon1 connecting with L2, four-subject expansion) still await the user's scheduling, not started.
